solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Action-led shot framing Coppola's first western

indicators.note: a shot thing is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled
the scrambled letters surround the next piece like a frame
take only the opening letter of Coppola

parts.note: first letter of Coppola, set inside the scrambled letters

explanation.surface: A film critic notes that Francis Ford Coppola's first western opened with an action-packed shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'western' a film genre, but the answer is the adjective: occidental means of the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental means belonging to the western part of the world.

clue.text: Fine area outside South American city

indicators.note: the letters for 'fine area' sit outside the next piece

parts.note: SA = South American, placed between the O and the KA

explanation.surface: Someone describes a pleasant district on the edge of a city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'South American city' as one phrase, but South American only supplies SA; the city is in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Osaka is one of Japan's largest cities, so 'city' covers it.

clue.text: Beastly noise — provide barrier for ears

indicators.note: what follows is meant for the ears, so take its sound

parts.note: a wall is a barrier; WAUL is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a dreadful racket and asks for something to protect their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrier for ears' looks like a request for earplugs, but 'for ears' only asks you to hear the barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterwaul is the wailing howl of a cat, a truly beastly noise.

clue.text: Selfish person one might cast in Jeopardy

indicators.note: letters that are cast are thrown into a new shape
the scrambled letters go inside the next word

parts.note: jeopardy = danger; it is split D...ANGER around the anagram

explanation.surface: A casting director wonders who could play the selfish character on the quiz show Jeopardy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeopardy looks like the TV quiz show, but it is just danger. A dog in the manger, from Aesop, keeps others from what it cannot use itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog in the manger is someone who spitefully withholds from others what they have no use for.

clue.text: De Gaulle's veto on return of lager designed to prevent accidents

parts.note: de Gaulle famously said 'non' to Britain joining the Common Market

indicators.note: the lager comes back, so its letters read backwards

parts.note: Pils is a pilsner lager; reversed it gives SLIP

explanation.surface: A history of de Gaulle vetoing the return of lager, framed as a safety measure.
explanation.walkthrough: De Gaulle's 'non' vetoed Britain's application to join the Common Market in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonslip surface or sole is designed to stop people slipping and having accidents.

clue.text: Charity officer's abysmal morale ending in depression

indicators.note: abysmal morale is in a terrible state, so its letters are rearranged
take only the final letter of depression

explanation.surface: A charity worker's spirits are so low they have sunk into depression.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 's stands for 'has': the charity officer has the letters that follow. An almoner originally handed out alms to the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner distributed alms, a charity officer in a monastery or great household.

clue.text: Painter of Henry V as a young man

parts.words: Henry V as a young man
parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
'of' read as the possessive ending 's attached to the prince

explanation.surface: A question about who painted the young Henry V.
explanation.walkthrough: Frans Hals was the Dutch portrait painter of The Laughing Cavalier. 'Of' is read as the possessive 's, turning HAL into HAL'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Frans Hals was a seventeenth-century Dutch painter.

clue.text: Deliberate inaccuracy in article from abroad

indicators.note: the lie goes inside the article

parts.note: AN is the indefinite article, split A...N
a lie is a deliberate inaccuracy

explanation.surface: A newspaper story from overseas contains a deliberate falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but here it is the grammatical article AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign, coming from abroad.

clue.text: National register for part of final course

parts.note: a roll is a register of names

explanation.surface: A national register kept for students on the last part of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final course' suggests the end of a training programme; it is the last course of a meal. A Swiss roll is a rolled sponge cake with jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll, a rolled sponge cake, can be served as part of dessert, the final course.

clue.text: For luxury dining, cook baked beans first, not second

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it into a new form, so rearrange the letters
the letter for 'second' is left out

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters before the deletion
s = second; remove one S, leaving 14 letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: for a fancy meal, cook the baked beans first rather than second.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a kitchen instruction, but 'cook' only tells you to rearrange the letters once an S is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast brought to you in bed is a classic indulgence, luxury dining.

clue.text: Invasive element's current information on American conservation society

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'on' puts the first pieces after the ones that follow

parts.note: NT = the National Trust, Britain's heritage and conservation charity
I is the symbol for electric current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An invasive species is described as a live issue for an American conservation group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'up to date', but it is the physics symbol I. The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic buildings and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a foreign substance that invades the body and triggers an immune response.

clue.text: Piece of film art initially displays something intoxicating

indicators.note: the answer is only a piece of the words that follow
the words put the answer on show inside themselves

explanation.surface: A film critic notes that a piece of art first shows something heady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but here it is just part of the text the answer sits in.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a gin or vodka cocktail, certainly intoxicating.

clue.text: Plug in hosts connected to revolutionary network: cause of power surge?

indicators.note: a revolutionary network is turned round, so its letters read backwards

parts.note: to plug a product is to advertise it; an ad is a plug
LAN = local area network; reversed it gives NAL

explanation.surface: An electrician's instructions for plugging hosts into a network, ending with a worry about a power surge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all electrics, but the power surge is a burst of energy in the body. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone behind a sudden surge of energy and strength.

clue.text: Woman's name in historical times

indicators.note: the letter for name goes inside the word for historical times

parts.note: ages = long historical periods, split AG...ES

explanation.surface: A remark that a woman's name is rooted in historical times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's name' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Woman' and 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Catch without licence, exchanging penny for river fish

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out
the penny is replaced by the river

parts.note: to poach is to catch game or fish illegally
r = river, the letter put in its place

explanation.surface: An angler caught fishing without a licence swaps a penny for a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River fish' reads as one phrase, but 'river' belongs to the wordplay and 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the roach is a common European freshwater species, so plain 'fish' covers it.

clue.text: Went back to see vicar I established in position

explanation.surface: Someone returned to see a vicar they had installed in his parish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one story, but 'established in position' is a single idea: placed somewhere, or sited.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the re- prefix supplies 'back' and visited supplies 'went to see'.

clue.text: Collection extracted from soil of tropics to the west

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the words that follow
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

explanation.surface: A set of samples taken from tropical soil to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the west' sounds like geography, but in an across clue it tells you to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a collection of works, documents or investments.

clue.text: Uninhibited live artist close to limit in song

indicators.note: the end of 'limit', its last letter

parts.note: a lied is a German art song, split LI...ED

indicators.note: these letters go inside the song

explanation.surface: A singer performing live pushes a song right to its limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like 'in concert', but it is the verb BE. A lied is a German song, a classical recital favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated means free of social inhibitions.

clue.text: Instrument used by Sparks?

parts.note: the surface wants a musical instrument; the setter means a measuring device
the surface suggests the pop band Sparks; the setter means Sparks, the traditional nickname for an electrician

explanation.surface: A question about what instrument the band Sparks plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparks looks like the name of a pop band, so 'instrument' suggests music; Sparks is also the old nickname for an electrician, whose instrument measures voltage.
explanation.definitionFit: A voltmeter measures electrical voltage, a tool an electrician would use.

clue.text: Thanks boyfriend, introducing beginning of love scene

indicators.note: the boyfriend takes a letter into himself

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: take the first letter of love

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend, split B...EAU

explanation.surface: A thank-you to a boyfriend for bringing a love scene into the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love scene' reads as one phrase, but 'love' only supplies its L and 'scene' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tableau is a striking scene, especially one frozen on stage like a picture.

clue.text: Parrot got up — everyone got up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A parrot flies up and everybody in the room rises with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' appears twice with two jobs: first it means ROSE, then it sends ALL upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The rosella is a brightly coloured Australian parrot.

clue.text: She predicts crux of inside line on Times

indicators.note: in an across clue, the line comes after the times
the crux is the heart, so take the middle letters

explanation.surface: A pundit forecasts the heart of an inside story published in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Times look like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world who foretold the future.

clue.text: Secretary bird keeps losing a lot of eggs

indicators.note: the bird holds the secretary inside
to lose something is to be left without it, so the A is taken away

explanation.surface: A secretary bird, the African bird of prey, keeps losing its eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secretary bird' is a real species, which hides the split. 'A lot of eggs' reads as a quantity, but 'a' belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn is the mass of eggs laid by fish or frogs.

clue.text: Collect degree taken by dimwit

indicators.note: the degree is taken inside the dimwit

parts.note: an ass is a fool, split A...SS

explanation.surface: A fool picks up a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: MA, Master of Arts, is the usual crossword degree; the joke is the dimwit earning one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to gather things together into a heap.

clue.text: Roused Democrat after closest associate embraces Republican Right

indicators.note: the Democrat comes after the rest
the closest associate holds the Rs inside

parts.note: a bestie is a best friend, split BESTI...E

explanation.surface: A Democrat is stirred up after his closest ally cosies up to the Republican right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closest associate' is the slang bestie, a best friend. The two Rs sit side by side because Republican and Right each give one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to bestir yourself is to rouse yourself into action.

clue.text: Romantic hero's bow in hollow display

indicators.note: 'in' places the bow within what follows, so its letters sit inside the emptied display
display with its middle scooped out leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: a bow is an arc shape

explanation.surface: A romantic hero takes his bow in an empty show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like the gesture of a hero taking a bow; it is the curved shape ARC. Mr Darcy is the hero of Pride and Prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Darcy is the romantic hero of Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Swinger's gin and ecstasy tablets reported

parts.note: a gin is a trap for catching animals

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so take the sound

parts.note: E = ecstasy; several E tablets are Es, said 'eez'

explanation.surface: A party-goer's gin and ecstasy pills are reported to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a party animal and gin suggests a drink; the swinger is a trapeze and the gin is an animal snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a swinging bar used by acrobats, literally a swinger.

clue.text: Creature caught in coastal waters — throw back with tail missing

indicators.note: the last letter of the back is cut off

parts.note: the stern is the back of a boat; without its last letter N it is STER

explanation.surface: A fisherman catches something in coastal waters and throws it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw back' reads as a phrase telling you to reverse something, but it is two separate words: LOB, then the stern of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobsters are crustaceans caught in pots in coastal waters.

clue.text: Record lives in centre of US politics

indicators.note: the letters for lives go inside

parts.note: Washington DC is the seat of US government, split D...C

explanation.surface: A record of people's lives at the heart of American politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of US politics' looks like a middle-letter instruction, but it is Washington DC, the seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from music: a vinyl record is a flat disc.

clue.text: Irregular guards carry golf bags without clubs for rich older guy

indicators.note: irregular guards are out of order, so rearrange them
the letter for clubs is left out

parts.note: to caddy is to carry a golfer's bags
C = clubs, the card suit; removed from CADDY to leave ADDY

explanation.surface: Irregular soldiers guard a caddy lugging golf bags with no clubs in them, all for a rich old man.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf surface makes 'clubs' look like golf clubs, but it is the card suit C.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is a rich older man who lavishes gifts on a younger partner.
